item.title: US pays $725 million to UN, easing its debt dispute with the world body
item.description: The Trump administration paid $725 million to the United Nations, the organization said on Wednesday, reducing Washington's large debt and ensuring it keeps its vote at the U.N. General Assembly convening in New York next week.
item.dc:creator: Antoni Slodkowski
item.content:encoded: The Trump administration paid $725 million to the United Nations, the organization said on Wednesday, reducing Washington's large debt and ensuring it keeps its vote at the U.N. General Assembly [USN:S0N43500V TEXT:"convening in New York"] next week. Trump has criticized the global body for not living up to its potential and slashed funding to many U.N. agencies. When asked about the planned payment last month, [USN:L6N44I0JV TEXT:"a U.S. official said"] any payments will be contingent on continued reforms of the U.N. "We received $725 million yesterday from the United States for the U.N. regular budget, and we also received $102 million from the U.S. for peacekeeping on Friday," said U.N. spokesperson Farhan Haq. "The U.S. still owes $1.312 billion to the regular budget," he said, adding that, "with these payments, the U.S. is no longer in jeopardy of falling under Article 19 for 2027." Under Article 19 of the U.N. Charter, a member state loses its voting rights in the General Assembly if its arrears exceed two years in annual fees, although grace periods are possible. The Trump administration has carried out an unprecedented shrinking of its federal government, saying it was bloated and has significantly cut back on domestic and foreign grants in an effort that it says was to put money into causes that aligned with U.S. taxpayer interests. The U.S. is the biggest contributor to the U.N. budget, but under the Trump administration it has slow-walked mandatory payments to regular and peacekeeping budgets, and has slashed voluntary funding to U.N. agencies with their own budgets. The second-biggest contributor, China, also paid $641.4 million on September 1 in its regular budget contributions, according to the U.N. website. The U.N. has been undergoing a reform and cost-cutting exercise known as "UN80" amid its financial crisis.

item.title: Caps re-sign F Justin Sourdif to 8-year, $50.8M deal
item.description: The Washington Capitals re-signed forward Justin Sourdif to an eight-year, $50.8 million contract.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Washington Capitals re-signed forward Justin Sourdif to an eight-year, $50.8 million contract. The deal was completed Tuesday, the last day teams were allowed to ink players to eight-year contracts. Sourdif, 24, had 35 points (15 goals, 20 assists) in 78 games of his 2025-26 rookie campaign with the Capitals. "Justin is a good young forward who has continued to develop steadily throughout his career. He is versatile and demonstrated his ability to play an important forward role for our team whenever the opportunity arose last season," general manager Chris Patrick said. "We are thrilled to sign him to a long-term contract and look forward to seeing him continue to elevate his game alongside our veteran core and our young group of players. We believe he has a bright future ahead of him and are confident that he will continue to make valuable contributions to our organization in the coming years." Sourdif finished third among NHL rookies in plus-minus rating (plus-17), tied for eighth in points and tied for 11th in goals. The Florida Panthers drafted the British Columbia native in the third round in 2020 and traded him to Washington in June 2025 for a 2026 second-round pick and a 2027 sixth-rounder. --Field Level Media

item.title: RWE buys 3% more in M31, lifts its Amprion stake to about 58%
item.description: RWE , Germany's biggest power producer, said on Wednesday it had bought an additional 3% stake in M31, which holds around three-quarters of shares in transmission system operator Amprion.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: RWE (RWEG.DE) , Germany's biggest power producer, said on Wednesday it had bought an additional 3% stake in M31, which holds around three-quarters of shares in transmission system operator Amprion. With the acquisition, RWE's pro-rata stake in Amprion will increase to about 58%, making it the majority shareholder of M31, RWE said. Here are more details: RWE said Amprion will remain an independent transmission operator, adding that it will consolidate its stake in Amprion at equity. Sources told Reuters earlier this year that Amprion's major owners were considering [USN:L8N3Z11QX TEXT:"selling"] their stakes to new investors. In July, Germany's Federal Cartel Office approved RWE's acquisition of about 47% of shares in M31. M31's shareholders include MEAG Munich Ergo, which is Munich Re's (MUVGn.DE) asset management arm, along with Swiss Life (SLHN.S) , Talanx (TLXGn.DE) , insurer Versicherungskammer and Commerzbank's (CBKG.DE) Commerz Real.

item.title: Heeney Capital firma un acuerdo para operar una mina en Venezuela y exportar el oro
item.description: La firma de inversión Heeney Capital, de Nueva York, firmó el miércoles un acuerdo con Venezuela que le otorga acceso a la codiciada mina Choco, en el país sudamericano, informó la compañía en una conferencia de prensa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La firma de inversión Heeney Capital, de Nueva York, firmó el miércoles un acuerdo con Venezuela que le otorga acceso a la codiciada mina Choco, en el país sudamericano, informó la compañía en una conferencia de prensa. Heeney se ha asociado con la comercializadora de materias primas Mercuria para este acuerdo de 30 años, el cual también concede a las empresas los derechos para exportar el oro extraído de la mina, indicó un portavoz de Heeney. La firma prevé una inversión inicial de hasta 1.000 millones de dólares en el proyecto. El acuerdo, suscrito en Houston con autoridades venezolanas, también considera la posibilidad de ampliar el contrato.

item.title: Satellite data shows major ice losses for Greenland and Antarctica
item.description: New research based on satellite data going back to the 1970s has documented major polar ice losses in Greenland and Antarctica — home to Earth's two great ice sheets — that have contributed to rising global sea levels.
item.dc:creator: Will Dunham
item.content:encoded: New research based on satellite data going back to the 1970s has documented major polar ice losses in Greenland and Antarctica — home to Earth's two great ice sheets — that have contributed to rising global sea levels. Between 1979 and 2023, according to data from 27 satellite missions, Greenland and Antarctica lost a combined 11.3 trillion tons of ice, adding 1.24 inches (3.14 cm) to the worldwide sea-level rise. The study, employing the longest satellite data record of changes in ice sheets ever gathered to give the most complete account to date of ice loss in Greenland and Antarctica, was conducted by the Ice Sheet Mass Balance Inter-comparison Exercise team, an international group of polar scientists. The findings, they said, offer fresh evidence of the effects of human-caused global climate change. "To put this very large number into context, 11.3 trillion tons of ice is enough ice to fill in a cube that would be 23 kilometers (14.3 miles) in height," said climate scientist Inès Otosaka of Northumbria University in England, lead author of the study published on Wednesday in the journal Scientific Data . Of the ice loss documented in the study, about 60% came from Greenland and 40% from Antarctica, even though Greenland is about one-eighth the size of Antarctica. "When ice sheets melt, they contribute to rising global sea levels. And with every additional centimeter of sea-level rise, about 2 to 3 million people are put at risk of annual coastal flooding. The ice sheets are now a major driver of sea-level rise, accounting for about 25% of all sea-level rise," Otosaka said. "We have extended our satellite data record backwards in time to the 1970s, and this confirms that ice losses started in the 1990s and have increased since then. Our assessment shows that the pace of ice loss increased by a factor of four between the 1980s and 2010s," Otosaka said. The study documented a slowdown in ice loss between 2020 and 2023, though the researchers said this appears to represent a short-term variation and not a reversal of the long-term trend. Unusually high snowfall across East Antarctica provided enough ice to offset some of the losses from glaciers elsewhere on Antarctica, while relatively mild summers in Greenland substantially lowered surface melting, they said. Some 84% of the ice lost came from glaciers flowing more quickly into the ocean rather than from ice melting at the surface, showing that the long-term trend is being driven by the response of the ice sheets to a warming ocean, Otosaka said. The researchers said the total sea-level rise attributed to the ice losses at Greenland and Antarctica may not sound like a huge number, but it puts another 6 to 9 million people at risk of coastal flooding and erosion globally. "These findings have implications for coastal planning, showing that we urgently need to develop plans for protecting coastal communities around the world from the impact of ice sheet melting," Otosaka said.

item.title: US bets heavy on Westinghouse fleet but cost hurdles loom
item.description: New federal financing for ten Westinghouse AP1000 reactors could boost the nuclear supply chain but promised reductions in costs and construction times will not be straightforward, experts told Reuters Events.
item.dc:creator: Neil Ford
item.content:encoded: The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) announced a $17.5 billion nuclear power supply chain loan program in June to support the goal of having ten 1.1 GW AP1000 reactors under construction by 2030, in pairs at five sites. Westinghouse and a utility or energy company will each be required to invest $500 million to jointly own each project. Building a fleet of AP1000s is a central plank of President Trump’s goal of quadrupling U.S. nuclear generating capacity to 400 GW by 2050, and would help boost power supplies for data centres. The financing will support the procurement of reactor vessels and steam generators, and could reduce construction costs and accelerate projects “by up to three years,” Energy Secretary Chris Wright said when he unveiled the initiative. Fleet scale early orders backed by DOE financing will allow manufacturers to pull schedules forward, said John MacQuarrie, President, Commercial Operations at BWXT. “Committing to 10 reactors gives suppliers the confidence to invest in tooling, add qualified production capacity and staff, and benefit from ‘repeat build’ learning,” MacQuarrie told Reuters Events. “All of that brings per unit costs down compared to one off projects,” he added. CHART: Forecast US nuclear power capacity Source: World Nuclear Association (WNA), 2026 It usually takes up to five years to procure long-lead items, “making them difficult to order until financing has been fully secured,” said Wood Mackenzie Research Analyst Andrew Kleiman. The loans will enable procurement prior to financial close, “so fabrication can occur parallel to licensing and site preparation,” Kleiman told Reuters Events. However, the scale of the cost benefits from serial production remains unproven as ten reactors of the same model have never been built over such a short period, analysts said. “The DOE’s approach – financing bulk orders of long-lead time reactor equipment – is both novel and strategically sound to advance multiple projects at once” but cost overruns could still occur given the lack of deployment experience, Ishyan Deshak Veluppillai, Senior Associate at global consultancy Capstone, told Reuters Events. Join us at Reuters Events Fusion Energy 2026 to network with 250+ leaders from the global fusion ecosystem. The U.S. has brought just 2.2 GW of entirely new-build nuclear capacity online over the past three decades, Vogtle 3 and 4 in Georgia – the only two AP1000 reactors ever built in the U.S. However, these contributed to the huge losses that drove Westinghouse into bankruptcy protection in 2017, alongside its similarly troubled V.C. Summer project in South Carolina. Bechtel took over construction of Vogtle 3 and 4, which came online in 2023 and 2024. The new AP1000 units at Vogtle 3 and 4 “were made possible largely because of support from the DOE and the federal government,” a spokesperson for Southern Company, which partially owns and operates the reactors, told Reuters Events. Potential partners The loan program follows from an $80 billion partnership with Westinghouse’s owners, Canada-based Cameco and Brookfield Asset Management announced in October 2025. Under the agreement the U.S. government would arrange financing and help secure permits for Westinghouse reactors in exchange for profit sharing. For exclusive nuclear insights, sign up to our newsletter. Westinghouse in July announced plans for an initial public offering (IPO). A spokesperson for Cameco told Reuters Events that the company could not make public comments ahead of the proposed IPO. But when the program was announced, Brookfield CEO Connor Teskey said that it would “materially accelerate the build-out of large-scale nuclear power generation” and serve as a catalyst for nuclear by “providing the certainty needed to enhance the domestic nuclear supply chain.” DOE said that “Westinghouse has signed letters of intent with seven potential partners, each with identified project sites,” but did not provide further details about the potential partnerships. CHART: US nuclear power capacity additions Source: Energy Information Administration (EIA), 2024 Capstone has identified five utilities that are likely candidates: Dominion, DTE Energy, WEC Energy, PSEG, and Entergy. But Kleiman said that Duke Energy, which has combined licenses (COLs) to develop two AP1000s at William States Lee III in South Carolina; and NextEra, which holds COLs for two AP1000s at Turkey Point in Florida are also well positioned to establish partnerships with Westinghouse. Utilities have avoided commenting directly on their potential participation in the program. However, in April, Entergy CEO Drew Marsh said his company was actively investigating new nuclear although cost challenges remain. Data centre operators are also potential partners because of their need for firm 24/7 power. Wood Mackenzie calculates that hyperscalers and nuclear generators have signed 16 GW of PPAs to date, including the 20-year PPAs signed by Microsoft and Meta with Constellation Energy and Vistra, respectively. These PPAs are helping finance upgrades and restarts, so “the next logical step is to finance new builds,” noted Veluppillai. Download our exclusive report on the latest funding leaps in fusion energy. DOE research in 2024 found that 115 out of the country’s 145 coal-fired power plant sites and 37 out of 54 nuclear plant sites have room for a least one new AP1000-sized power plant. Siting new reactors on brownfield sites would offer “a reduced licensing burden and lower grid connection risk,” Kleiman said. The planned AP1000 builds "will inevitably rely on a small supplier base" that would include companies that are already part of Westinghouse's supply chain network, such as Doosan Enerbility and BWXT Canada, Kleiman said. Other existing Westinghouse partners, such as Hyundai, Bechtel Corporation, and Curtiss-Wright are also likely to play a role, noted Veluppillai.

item.title: OpenAI plays $1.5 trln chicken with chatbot frenzy
item.description: The ChatGPT maker is taking funding pitches to lift its valuation to 13 digits. The company wants more, as it rides a boost from its new model. Leaving less upside for new investors, while safety and economic risks balloon, is a tough sell even by crazed AI standards.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Guilford
item.content:encoded: The ChatGPT maker is taking funding pitches to lift its valuation to 13 digits. The company wants more, as it rides a boost from its new model. Leaving less upside for new investors, while safety and economic risks balloon, is a tough sell even by crazed AI standards. Full view will be published shortly. Follow Jonathan Guilford on X and LinkedIn . CONTEXT NEWS OpenAI has held conversations with investors about a new funding round that could value it at $1.2 trillion after they approached the company, the Financial Times reported on September 15. The ChatGPT developer believes it should be valued at $1.5 trillion at least, the New York Times subsequently reported on September 16, given advances in its latest AI models.

item.title: Texas ‘suspense’ voters are not disqualified, can confirm address and vote
item.description: A provision to verify voters’ addresses in their registration records has been misrepresented online to claim that Texas has suspended over a million voters from voting ahead of the U.S. Senate election on November 3.
item.dc:creator: Reuters Fact Check
item.content:encoded: A provision to verify voters’ addresses in their registration records has been misrepresented online to claim that Texas has suspended over a million voters from voting ahead of the U.S. Senate election on November 3. Democratic Senate candidate James Talarico, a state representative and former seminary student, will face Republican Ken Paxton, the state's attorney general, in a [USN:L6N44T0XY TEXT:"close race"]. An August 29 X post said, “BREAKING: Texas has suspended over one million voters ahead of the Senate race. This comes as James Talarico leads in statewide polling.” However, a spokesperson for the Texas Secretary of State told Reuters in an email that voters on the state’s “suspense” list can update their address before the October 5 deadline to vote in the November election, adding that some eligible voters who moved within the same county can complete a Statement of Residence in their former precinct. According to the Texas Secretary of State’s website, there are 1,228,918 suspense voters across the state. However, this does not mean these voters have been permanently suspended or disqualified from voting. The spokesperson said the suspense list was created in response to the National Voter Registration Act implemented in 1995 to protect voters’ ability to cast a ballot and maintain accurate voting rolls. “The number on the list is consistent with what we’ve seen at this stage of the election cycle,” the spokesperson said, adding that, if county election officials have reason to believe a voter has moved, often because of a returned voter registration card, they are added to the list. The FAQ page on the state’s official voting resources website says the same, adding detailed instructions for voters who have moved within the same county or to a different county to update their records. Jennifer Morrell, CEO and co-founder of The Elections Group, a nonpartisan organization that partners with state and local election officials in addressing operational challenges, said in an email that this is a routine process and it does not cancel a voter’s registration. Morrell added that the voter can fix the problem by updating their address in accordance with state laws and requirements. Christopher Mann, research director at the Center for Election Innovation & Research, also said in an email that the suspense list was a legally required routine and voters on the list can vote. Most other states refer to these records as "inactive" and “states have been implementing this law for three decades, and there is nothing unusual or new about the suspense list for Texas in 2026,” Mann said. VERDICT Misleading. Texas has not suspended more than a million voters; they are still registered to vote in the state and can do so after following procedures to correct the issue with their address. This article was produced by the Reuters Fact Check team. Read more about our fact-checking work.

item.title: Las acciones europeas suben mientras el petróleo se estabiliza, a la espera de la Fed
item.description: Las acciones europeas subieron el miércoles desde el mínimo de tres meses tocado en la víspera, ya que una pausa del alza del precio del petróleo impulsó el apetito por el riesgo, a la espera de la decisión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal, que podría anunciar su primera subida de tasas de interés desde 2023.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: Las acciones europeas subieron el miércoles desde el mínimo de tres meses tocado en la víspera, ya que una pausa del alza del precio del petróleo impulsó el apetito por el riesgo, a la espera de la decisión de política monetaria de la Reserva Federal, que podría anunciar su primera subida de tasas de interés desde 2023. * El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) ganó un 0,5%, a 637,09 puntos, y los principales índices nacionales también cerraron con ganancias. * Según la herramienta FedWatch de CME, los operadores ven una probabilidad del 93% de que haya una subida de 25 puntos básicos en las tasas, la primera bajo la presidencia de Kevin Warsh. * "Aunque es razonable que la Fed adopte una actitud de esperar y ver antes de subir las tasas, se ha mostrado firme en lo que respecta a la inflación. Si no actúa, su credibilidad podría verse afectada", dijo Kathleen Brooks, de XTB. "En nuestra opinión, Warsh se ha metido en un callejón sin salida en lo que respecta a las tasas". * Los riesgos de inflación derivados del conflicto con Irán han obligado a los inversores a reevaluar las perspectivas de las tasas, lo que ha impulsado al alza el rendimiento de los bonos en el mundo y ha ejercido presión sobre los activos de mayor riesgo. * El Banco Central Europeo subió las tasas por segunda vez este año la semana pasada, y los mercados siguen esperando otro incremento más de 25 puntos básicos este año, según datos de LSEG. * Sin embargo, el crecimiento salarial en la zona euro volvió a ralentizarse el último trimestre, mientras que los acuerdos salariales negociados apuntan a una recuperación solo moderada el año que viene, lo que tranquiliza a los responsables políticos al confirmar que el aumento de los precios sigue bajo control. * Las acciones del sector energético (.SXEP) fueron las que más cayeron, mientras que el sector de viajes y ocio (.SXTP) subió un 1,2%, ya que la perspectiva de unos menores costos del combustible ofreció cierto apoyo. Los papeles bancarios (.SX7P) avanzaron un 0,5%, recuperando parte de las pérdidas del martes.

item.title: American Airlines advierte de que alza del combustible podría obligar a realizar ajustes
item.description: El presidente ejecutivo de American Airlines, Robert Isom, dijo el miércoles que los precios del combustible, que se mantienen altos, podrían obligar a la aerolínea a ajustar su capacidad, a pesar de que la fuerte demanda y el aumento de los ingresos han ayudado a compensar gran parte del incremento de los costos .
item.dc:creator: Rajesh Singh, Shivansh Tiwary
item.content:encoded: El presidente ejecutivo de American Airlines, Robert Isom, dijo el miércoles que los precios del combustible, que se mantienen altos, podrían obligar a la aerolínea a ajustar su capacidad, a pesar de que la fuerte demanda y el aumento de los ingresos han ayudado a compensar gran parte del incremento de los costos . En su intervención en una conferencia de Morgan Stanley, Isom dijo sentirse "muy optimista" respecto de la previsión de crecimiento de los ingresos de American (AAL.O) para el tercer trimestre, que se sitúa entre el 16% y el 19%, y espera que la gran mayoría de las alzas resulten duraderas. Los comentarios ponen de relieve la presión a la que se ven sometidas las aerolíneas, ya que una nueva subida de los precios del combustible pone a prueba hasta qué punto el aumento de los costos puede seguir compensándose con unos ingresos más sólidos. American dice que, hasta ahora, ha recuperado una parte sustancial del incremento, pero el último repunte está obligando a realizar ajustes de capacidad para finales del cuarto trimestre. Isom señaló que el buen desempeño de los ingresos se ha generalizado tanto en los mercados nacionales como en los internacionales, y tanto en la clase premium como en la turista. American ya ha recuperado "una cantidad enorme" del aumento de los gastos de combustible gracias a los ingresos, agregó. Describió la mejora interanual actual de los ingresos como algo sin precedentes en toda su carrera, salvo las recuperaciones tras la pandemia de la COVID-19 y los atentados del 11 de septiembre. En la misma conferencia, el presidente financiero de American, Devon May, señaló que los precios del combustible en el cuarto trimestre habían subido cerca de 1 dólar por galón frente al nivel previsto cuando publicaron sus previsiones en julio, lo que supone un incremento de los costos de combustible de unos 1.000 millones de dólares. May señaló que cada variación de 1 centavo en los precios del combustible modifica los costos trimestrales de la compañía en unos 10 millones de dólares. La aerolínea seguirá ajustando su capacidad a finales del cuarto trimestre debido al aumento, añadió.

item.title: Pereira, do BCE, diz que inflação ainda não está se disseminando como no passado
item.description: A inflação na zona do euro não está se disseminando tão amplamente quanto em episódios anteriores, mas os formuladores de política estão acompanhando de perto a evolução da situação, especialmente à luz do recente aumento nos preços do gás, afirmou o presidente do banco central de Portugal, Álvaro Santos Pereira.
item.dc:creator: Marc Jones
item.content:encoded: A inflação na zona do euro não está se disseminando tão amplamente quanto em episódios anteriores, mas os formuladores de política estão acompanhando de perto a evolução da situação, especialmente à luz do recente aumento nos preços do gás, afirmou o presidente do banco central de Portugal, Álvaro Santos Pereira. “A inflação não está se espalhando nem se ampliando tão rapidamente como aconteceu em 2022”, disse Pereira, que integra o Conselho do BCE, em um evento do Centro Europeu de Economia e Finanças na Embaixada de Portugal em Londres. “Isso não significa que isso não possa acontecer... É importante para nós estarmos atentos, e vamos acompanhar de perto exatamente isso nos próximos meses para ver se a inflação está se disseminando.” O BCE elevou as taxas de juros da zona do euro na semana passada pela segunda vez neste ano, e os mercados financeiros estão precificando pelo menos mais três aumentos nos próximos 12 meses. Pereira disse que o aumento nos preços do gás natural era um dos fatores que ele estava acompanhando mais de perto, acrescentando que o boom da IA e seu impacto no crescimento global e na inflação eram outro “choque” com o qual os banqueiros centrais estavam lidando. “Há muitos riscos que certamente aumentaram nos últimos meses”, disse ele.

item.title: IA da OpenAI testou vulnerabilidades da Hugging Face meses antes de ataque
item.description: Agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI invadiram contas de usuários do Hugging Face e vasculharam o próprio site em busca de vulnerabilidades dois meses antes da invasão aos sistemas do repositório de software de código aberto em julho, segundo pesquisadores que analisaram a atividade.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter, Deepa Seetharaman
item.content:encoded: Agentes de inteligência artificial da OpenAI invadiram contas de usuários do Hugging Face e vasculharam o próprio site em busca de vulnerabilidades dois meses antes da invasão aos sistemas do repositório de software de código aberto em julho, segundo pesquisadores que analisaram a atividade. A OpenAI já havia divulgado um aspecto da atividade, o roubo das credenciais digitais de um usuário do Hugging Face para acessar um arquivo relacionado à biologia, em seu relatório público de incidentes no mês passado, mas pesquisadores afirmaram que a atividade de sondagem contra o site pareceu ir além do que o relatório descrevia. O pesquisador independente Jonas Wiedermann-Moeller disse à Reuters que descobriu a atividade na semana passada. Ele afirmou ter encontrado evidências de que os agentes da OpenAI comprometeram duas contas de usuários do Hugging Face e as utilizaram para enviar arquivos com formatação incomum aos servidores da empresa já em 13 de maio. Ele e outros pesquisadores que analisaram as evidências afirmaram que o comportamento se assemelhou a uma tentativa de mapear ou testar partes da rede da Hugging Face em busca de formas de infiltração, embora tenham enfatizado que não havia evidências de que a iniciativa tivesse resultado em uma violação efetiva. Tanto os pesquisadores quanto a OpenAI afirmaram não terem encontrado evidências de que essa sondagem anterior fizesse parte do incidente de julho. O porta-voz da OpenAI, Drew Pusateri, disse que a empresa havia divulgado o evento de 13 de maio no relatório de incidente, notificado a Hugging Face em particular sobre a atividade sinalizada por Wiedermann-Moeller e estava “comprometida com a transparência sobre essas questões e com o compartilhamento do que aprendermos à medida que nossa análise continua”. A Hugging Face, que recentemente fez acordo para ser comprada pela fabricante de chips Nvidia (NVDA.O) , não comentou o assunto. Wiedermann-Moeller, de 27 anos, que mora em Bielefeld, na Alemanha, disse que a falha da OpenAI em detectar a tentativa de invasão de 13 de maio naquele momento foi uma oportunidade perdida de impedir a campanha de hacking subsequente, que desencadeou uma reflexão global sobre o poder da inteligência artificial. “Imagine se eles tivessem detectado esse comportamento em maio”, disse ele em entrevista. “Isso poderia ter evitado o incidente posterior, que foi muito maior.” A OpenAI já havia afirmado anteriormente que, em retrospecto, “alguns sinais iniciais” de seus agentes de IA deveriam ter desencadeado uma resposta mais precoce. "SINAL DE ALERTA CLARO" Dois especialistas externos que analisaram as descobertas de Wiedermann-Moeller afirmaram que elas eram consistentes com atividades anteriormente associadas aos agentes da OpenAI. Tom Hegel, pesquisador sênior de ameaças da SentinelOne, disse que o sequestro da conta e as tentativas de sondagem subsequentes corresponderam “perfeitamente” ao comportamento conhecido dos agentes, afirmando em seu próprio relatório sobre o incidente que os laboratórios de IA de ponta deveriam divulgar mais dados sobre incidentes em que os agentes “interagem com ou afetam sistemas de terceiros”. Sydney Von Arx, do Nightingale Collective, um grupo dedicado à segurança da IA, também concordou com a atribuição. Von Arx disse que o ataque representou um “claro sinal de alerta” que poderia ter ajudado a evitar a violação ocorrida em julho. A OpenAI tem enfrentado críticas cada vez maiores desde que a empresa divulgou, em 21 de julho, que agentes de IA rebeldes contornaram controles internos, acessaram a internet aberta e coordenaram ações que a companhia descreveu como “um incidente cibernético sem precedentes”. Desde então, pesquisadores externos identificaram incidentes adicionais que supostamente envolvem agentes ligados à OpenAI, incluindo atividades que afetaram um site wiki alemão inativo e o repositório de pacotes de software RubyGems. A OpenAI reconheceu alguns desses incidentes somente depois que eles foram divulgados publicamente por terceiros. Duas fontes a par do assunto afirmaram que, no caso do RubyGems, os funcionários da OpenAI só perceberam que sua IA era responsável pela atividade maliciosa depois que o Nightingale Collective a descobriu. Essas novas descobertas alimentaram questionamentos entre parlamentares e defensores da segurança da IA sobre se toda a extensão dos incidentes já foi identificada. Desde então, alguns dos principais executivos de IA dos EUA têm pedido uma desaceleração no desenvolvimento da IA, citando, entre outras coisas, a ameaça de ataques por agentes fora de controle. Wiedermann-Moeller disse que as últimas descobertas reforçaram os apelos por uma desaceleração temporária no desenvolvimento de sistemas avançados de IA. “Uma pausa pode fazer bem ao mundo”, disse ele, “para que a questão da segurança possa acompanhar o ritmo”.

item.title: Ações sobem enquanto petróleo dá pausa antes de decisão do Fed sobre juros
item.description: As ações europeias subiram nesta quarta-feira em relação à mínima de três meses da sessão anterior, uma vez que uma pausa na alta dos preços do petróleo impulsionou o apetite por risco antes da decisão de política monetária do Federal Reserve, com ampla expectativa de que o banco central dos EUA anuncie o primeiro aumento de juros desde 2023.
item.dc:creator: Sudeshna Ghoshal, Ragini Mathur
item.content:encoded: As ações europeias subiram nesta quarta-feira em relação à mínima de três meses da sessão anterior, uma vez que uma pausa na alta dos preços do petróleo impulsionou o apetite por risco antes da decisão de política monetária do Federal Reserve, com ampla expectativa de que o banco central dos EUA anuncie o primeiro aumento de juros desde 2023. O índice pan-europeu STOXX 600 (.STOXX) subiu 0,5%, para 637,09 pontos. Os operadores estão precificando uma probabilidade de 93% de um aumento de 25 pontos-base na taxa de juros dos EUA, de acordo com a ferramenta FedWatch da CME, a primeira alta sob o comando de Kevin Warsh no Fed. “Embora seja razoável que o Fed adote uma postura de esperar para ver antes de aumentar os juros, ele tem se mostrado firme em relação à inflação. Se não agir, sua credibilidade poderá ser abalada”, disse Kathleen Brooks, diretora de pesquisa da XTB. “Em nossa opinião, Warsh se colocou em uma situação difícil em relação aos juros”, acrescentou ela. Os riscos de inflação decorrentes do conflito no Irã forçaram os investidores a reavaliar as perspectivas para as taxas de juros, elevando os rendimentos dos títulos globais e pressionando os ativos de maior risco. O Banco Central Europeu elevou os juros pela segunda vez neste ano na semana passada, e os mercados ainda esperam outro aumento de 25 pontos-base até o final do ano, de acordo com dados da LSEG. Os preços do petróleo caíram quase 1% após um aumento inesperadamente grande nos estoques de petróleo bruto dos EUA, apesar das contínuas interrupções no abastecimento no Oriente Médio. As ações de energia (.SXEP) foram as que mais caíram no STOXX 600, enquanto o setor de viagens e lazer (.SXTP) registrou alta de 1,2%, já que a perspectiva de custos mais baixos com combustível ofereceu algum suporte. Em LONDRES, o índice Financial Times (.FTSE) avançou 0,28%, a 10.688,47 pontos. Em FRANKFURT, o índice DAX (.GDAXI) subiu 0,53%, a 25.537,75 pontos. Em PARIS, o índice CAC-40 (.FCHI) ganhou 0,62%, a 8.140,59 pontos. Em MILÃO, o índice Ftse/Mib (.FTMIB) teve valorização de 0,80%, a 51.969,12 pontos. Em MADRI, o índice Ibex-35 (.IBEX) registrou alta de 0,41%, a 19.635,80 pontos. Em LISBOA, o índice PSI20 (.PSI20) valorizou-se 1,00%, a 9.540,66 pontos.

item.title: Ghana Gas to decide on $500 million gas pipeline early next year, CEO says
item.description: State-owned Ghana Gas plans to make a final investment decision by early next year on a long-discussed $500 million pipeline project that would send supply from its gas processing plant in the western part of the country to industries in the southeast, CEO Judith Adjobah Blay said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Florence Tan
item.content:encoded: State-owned Ghana Gas plans to make a final investment decision by early next year on a long-discussed $500 million pipeline project that would send supply from its gas processing plant in the western part of the country to industries in the southeast, CEO Judith Adjobah Blay said on Wednesday. The proposed 278-kilometre (173-mile) West-East onshore pipeline will enable the company to meet growing industrial sector demand and reduce its reliance on the West African pipeline shared by neighbouring countries, Blay told Reuters on the sidelines of the Gastech conference. "It's a project that we hope to really embark on by the end of the first quarter of 2027," she said, as the company is trying to line up financing. The project has been under discussion for nearly a decade, as Ghana seeks cheaper and more reliable gas supplies to power industries in the Tema industrial enclave. The plan would be for the government to take a 30% stake in the pipeline, while the rest would be funded by private firms, she added. Ghana Gas expects to receive more gas from the Eni-operated offshore Sankofa project when its production increases to 350 million standard cubic feet per day (mmscfd) in 2028, Blay said, up from 280 mmscfd currently. The company processes about 130 mmscfd of associated gas from the Tullow-operated Jubilee and TEN oil fields, she said. The fields have an extra 50 mmscfd of gas available, which will be processed at a proposed gas processing plant that needs lawmaker approval before more details can be announced, Blay said. Ghana's gas consumption is forecast to reach 715 mmscfd by 2030, up from 502 mmscfd this year, according to the company. Ghana imports 70 mmscfd of lean gas from Nigeria, she said. "The policy is to use gas primarily for power production," she said, as that would reduce the need to burn costlier fuels.

item.title: Novartis halts ALS drug development after mid-stage trial failure
item.description: Novartis has halted development of an experimental drug for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis after it failed to meet goals in a mid-stage study, marking the latest disappointment for the Swiss drugmaker this year.
item.dc:creator: Sriparna Roy
item.content:encoded: Novartis (NOVN.S) has halted development of an experimental drug for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis after it failed to meet goals in a mid-stage study, marking the latest disappointment for the Swiss drugmaker this year. This [USN:L4N4510T5 TEXT:"follows"] an earlier setback for a closely watched heart drug, last week's late-stage failure of a muscle-wasting drug, and the halt of eight of 10 studies for its rap-cel cell therapy this month after three patient deaths. These developments have intensified [USN:L8N4511SB TEXT:"investor"] scrutiny of its pipeline. Endpoints News and Bloomberg News reported the news earlier on Wednesday, which the company later confirmed in an emailed statement to Reuters, saying it was discontinuing development of the drug VHB937. The drug, also called lifonebart, was being studied in patients with ALS, also called Lou Gehrig's disease. It is a neurodegenerative condition that affects how nerve cells communicate with muscles and leads to muscle weakness that worsens over time. The company's U.S.-listed shares were marginally up. The drug failed to meet both main and secondary goals in the mid-stage trial, which was evaluating the efficacy and safety of VHB937 in participants with early-stage ALS within two years of symptom onset. The study had enrolled 251 patients, according to clinicaltrials.gov. The drug aims to stabilize TREM2, a protein that helps regulate immune responses, inflammation and waste clearance in the brain. Companies have been trying to develop TREM2 drug candidates but have faced failures. In 2024, Alector (ALEC.O) said its experimental drug failed in a mid-stage trial. Novartis is also studying the drug in patients with Alzheimer's disease, a progressive brain disorder that slowly robs memory. The clinical trials website shows the company is recruiting patients for the mid-stage trial.

item.title: Twins place SS Kaelen Culpepper (hamstring) on IL

item.content:encoded: The Minnesota Twins placed rookie shortstop Kaelen Culpepper on the 10-day injured list on Wednesday with a left hamstring strain. Culpepper, 23, was removed from Tuesday night's 8-1 loss to the New York Yankees in the top of the seventh inning. The Twins' 2024 first-round draft pick has batted .275 with three homers and 11 RBIs in 31 games since making his major league debut on Aug. 7. Culpepper also batted .271 with 14 homers, 46 RBIs and 17 stolen bases in 74 games at Triple-A St. Paul this season. The Twins recalled infielder Ben Ross from St. Paul in a corresponding move. Ross, 25, made his MLB debut on Sept. 1 and was 0-for-4 with one run scored and three strikeouts in three games with Minnesota in his first stint with the Twins. --Field Level Media

item.title: India pick Kohli, Rohit for West Indies ODIs; Nigam joins Asian Games squad
item.description: Stalwarts Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma headline India's One-Day International squad for their upcoming home series against the West Indies, while Vipraj Nigam has replaced injured spinner Varun Chakaravarthy in the Asian Games squad.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Stalwarts Virat Kohli and Rohit Sharma headline India's One-Day International squad for their upcoming home series against the West Indies, while Vipraj Nigam has replaced injured spinner Varun Chakaravarthy in the Asian Games squad. Top-order batter Shubman Gill will captain India in the three-match ODI series, with wicketkeeper-batter KL Rahul named vice-captain, while batting all-rounder Naman Dhir and bowler Auqib Nabi have earned their maiden ODI call-ups. The ODI series begins in Thiruvananthapuram, Kerala, on September 27. For the Twenty20 series against the West Indies, 15-year-old prodigy Vaibhav Sooryavanshi has been included in the squad led by top-order batter Shreyas Iyer. India will play five T20 internationals against the West Indies, starting in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh, on October 6. India will also play a one-off T20 international against Japan on September 22, before beginning their Asian Games campaign at the quarter-final stage six days later. Chakaravarthy has been ruled out of both the Japan T20 and the Asian Games with a side strain. All-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, who was originally named in the Asian Games squad, has been withdrawn and included in the ODI squad for the West Indies series instead. All-rounder Hardik Pandya and wicketkeeper-batter Rishabh Pant are notable absentees from India's squads for the West Indies ODI and T20 series, the Japan T20 and the Asian Games.
